warnings: Reframe/recompose so the window and impact point are the hero (impact should fill ~30–50% of frame). Remove/raise the foreground obstruction and move the camera closer/lower.

Increase overall scene illumination and motivated keys so glass can read in darkness; specifically raise background/world intensity (Line 274: bg.inputs['Strength'] from 0.08 → ~0.25–0.6) and adjust exposure so blacks aren’t crushing the action.

Make the glass material read more physically: keep metallic at 0 (Line 131), and consider slightly increasing roughness only if highlights are noisy (Line 154: 0.015 → ~0.02–0.04) while ensuring strong, clean reflections.
Reduce overly strong green tint if it’s muddying the shards: lower absorption density (Line 164: 0.12 → ~0.03–0.08) and/or neutralize absorption color (Line 163) for clearer shard readability.
Add subtle micro-surface breakup to help specular sparkle: increase bump strength a bit (Line 128) and tune noise scale (Line 120) so glass isn’t perfectly CG-smooth, but avoid heavy distortion.
If emission is contributing to a non-photoreal look, keep it minimal/disabled for realism (Line 178: emission strength → 0 or very low). Use lighting instead of glowing glass.

Increase fracture/shard resolution and drive higher initial shard velocity + angular spin (simulation/fracture settings, not in the listed material params): you need a clear radial crack pattern + wide debris spread from the impact point, plus remaining cracked glass still attached to the frame that collapses later.
Improve set realism (beyond current material params): add rusted steel frame detail, aged concrete texture variation, grime, and industrial dressing; right now it reads too geometric and empty.
Address render noise with higher samples/denoising (render settings), especially because dark scenes amplify grain.
Add motion cues if this is part of an animation (motion blur on brick/shards, directional debris spread from left-to-center impact) so the event reads as high-speed and violent.
